compatibility.linuxQt: v1 writer + separate TS + muxed TS segments + growing TS + separate fMP4 H264/AAC + WebM VP9/Opus

initialCorrections: The first fault fixture ended one byte before the first complete mdat, so opening correctly returned waiting_initialization. The healthy baseline now includes the first fragment and one byte of the next moof.

The first Windows MSVC fault run assumed an open resource could be replaced, and exited 1 on OS PermissionError. The test now proves Windows denies replacement while pinned, preserves valid reads and permits replacement after release. Linux proves detection of a completed replacement. Final runs on all four toolchains passed.
limitations: Exactly two required scalar AVC/AAC views of one head-moov fragmented resource, explicit first-trun offsets and default-base-is-moof; no segment catalog, additional tracks, muxed WebM or other muxed codecs.
Each virtual view retains the whole shared mdat; prefetch may perform extra reads. Multi-hour throughput, maximum index capacity and worst-case memory have not been stress-tested.
Container/index validation is not full elementary-stream entropy validation; actual codecs remain authoritative.
Native decoded hashes and exact timestamp comparison do not measure physical output synchronization.
Windows application builds were tested with separate profiles; installed Windows EXEs/INIs were not replaced.
